subject: Trial framework & model selection for Vendix pilot
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice@vendix.co>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Trial framework: proposed scope, success criteria, and model options

Hi Alice / team —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call earlier. Per our conversation, I captured a compact trial framework to get us to a go/no-go for production in ~4 weeks. Please see the attached trial-charter.xlsx and the quick bullets below. If anything looks off, call it out and we’ll update.

High-level goal
- Validate an LLM-based assistant to handle customer onboarding flows (web + in-app chat) with intent routing to 5 core intents and secure handling of PII.

Primary success criteria (proposed)
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for typical 128-token exchange
- Cost: inference cost <= $0.45 per 1k tokens (target for trial)
- Quality: intent precision >= 90% on curated prompt set; top-1 resolution rate >= 85%
- Hallucination: < 2% critical hallucinations on domain prompts (critical = legal/contract answers)
- Security/compliance: no customer data stored in logs outside your region; audit log capture for all requests

Model recommendations (initial) — open model focus
- Primary: Mistral-Instruct-22B (good instruction-following + latency/cost tradeoff on our infra)
- Primary fallback: Llama2-Chat-7B (Q4 quantized variant) for low-latency bursts and cost cap scenarios
- Multilingual fallback: BLOOMZ-7B for Portuguese/Spanish edge cases (we’ll selectively route low-confidence non-English requests)

Ownership and roles
- Mina (me): overall trial owner / exec contact
- Ben: infra + dedicated endpoint config, autoscaling policies, quantization profiles
- Monica: eval lead — prompt set, scoring rubric, and acceptance testing

Proposed timeline (4 weeks)
- Week 0 (this week): finalize criteria, confirm model choices, sign SOW stub
- Week 1: infra provisioning + model onboarding + prompt set collection
- Week 2: internal tuning and first-run metrics + customer demo
- Week 3: acceptance test, security checklist, and final adjustments
- Week 4: trial closeout report and recommendation

Open items for Vendix
- Confirm languages in scope (we noted English + Spanish + Portuguese during call)
- Confirm procurement/PO window and any data residency constraints
- Share a prioritized list of 50 representative prompts (we attached eval-prompt-set.csv to help)

Next steps
- Alice: confirm languages + procurement contact by Tue 2026-08-03
- We: produce an SOW stub (attached redwood-poc-sow.pdf) and updated charter after your confirmation

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly.

—
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: trial-charter.xlsx, eval-prompt-set.csv, redwood-poc-sow.pdf

Date: Sun, 2 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial framework: proposed scope, success criteria, and model options

Thanks Mina — this is very helpful and close to what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Languages: we definitely need English + Spanish (ES-ES) and Portuguese (pt-BR) for the top customer segments. Spanish is the priority after English.
2) Data residency: for this pilot we need all logs and audit traces to remain in us-east-1. For production we’ll evaluate cross-region options but trial must stay in our region.
3) Procurement: our procurement lead (procure@vendix.co) is looped. We have a two-week PO window but can expedite if SOW is straightforward.
4) Security: we’ll send our standard security questionnaire (SOC2 + data handling) by tomorrow — expect it from Jorge.

Model note: we want to avoid any model that consistently hallucinates on contract language. If Mistral-Instruct-22B works well for English, are we able to run the Spanish/Portuguese prompts through the same model or do you recommend separate routing? Also curious about the fallback behavior if latency spikes.

Happy to confirm languages and procurement once our security team sends the questionnaire. Appreciate the clear owners — will try to have the 50 prompts by Tue.

Best,
Alice
Director of Product, Vendix
alice@vendix.co

Hi Alice / Jorge / team —

Thanks — noted on the PO window and region constraint. Quick replies to the two asks:

1) Multilingual approach
- Primary strategy: try a single primary model (Mistral-Instruct-22B) for English and Spanish where it meets latency/quality targets. In our experience Mistral variants handle Spanish reasonably well but we’ll measure on your prompts.
- Fallback routing: if model confidence < threshold (we’ll propose 0.75) OR latency SLA is at risk, route to Llama2-Chat-7B (Q4 quantized) for faster response and cost fallback. For low-confidence Portuguese prompts we’ll route to BLOOMZ-7B as a safety net.

2) Hallucination and contract language
- Mitigation: prompt-level guardrails, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) against your contract snippets, and classifier-based verification on legal/contract answers. We’ll run the legal prompt set through a hallucination audit during Week 2.

3) Quantitative acceptance (finalize with Monica) — proposed thresholds for acceptance testing:
- Intent precision >= 90% (measured on seeded test set)
- Response latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms
- Cost: average inference cost <= $0.45 per 1k tokens across test set
- Critical hallucinations: < 2%

Ownership (explicit)
- Mina: trial owner and vendor exec touchpoint
- Ben: endpoint provisioning, model variant setup, autoscaling, logging & region controls (us-east-1 only for trial)
- Monica: test rubric, scoring scripts, collating results + acceptance verdict

Milestones (adjusted)
- Tue 2026-08-04: Vendix confirms languages + shares procurement lead PO timeline + initial 50 prompts
- Thu 2026-08-06: Redwood provides SOW stub and trial endpoint details
- Mon 2026-08-10: First tuning run + initial metrics report
- Fri 2026-08-14: Acceptance test and trial readout

Attachments: updated eval-prompt-set.csv (we added language tags)

If this looks good we’ll draft the SOW stub and lock in infra on Wed. Ben — can you confirm we can enforce us-east-1 logging and the quantized fallback config?

—
Mina
